findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] No plaintext or fast-hashed credential storage and no naive equality comparison is present. The passlib CryptContext at lines 17-23 lists argon2 (argon2id) first so every new hash uses it, with cost parameters pinned to the OWASP guidance (time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536 KiB, parallelism=4) rather than left to library defaults, and bcrypt retained at rounds=12 for verification only with deprecated='auto' driving migration. get_password_hash at line 45 and create_user at line 142 persist only the derived hash, which carries a per-password salt. Verification goes through pwd_context.verify and verify_and_update (lines 32 and 42), both constant-time inside passlib, and authenticate_user returns the same bare False for an unknown user, a locked account and a wrong password (lines 94, 101, 110) so the caller emits one generic 401. verify_and_upgrade_password re-hashes legacy bcrypt entries at login, the only moment the plaintext exists. No sha256, md5 or sha1 digest call and no '==' comparison against a stored credential appears in the file | verdict=pass confidence=high
